title.en: Human capital: meaning, and physical vs human capital
title.kn: ಮಾನವ ಬಂಡವಾಳ: ಅರ್ಥ, ಭೌತಿಕ ಮತ್ತು ಮಾನವ ಬಂಡವಾಳ

hook.en: A factory buys a new machine; a family pays for a daughter to become a doctor. Both are investments that raise future output. In what way are they different?
hook.kn: ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆ ಹೊಸ ಯಂತ್ರ ಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ; ಕುಟುಂಬ ಮಗಳನ್ನು ವೈದ್ಯೆಯಾಗಿಸಲು ಖರ್ಚು ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಎರಡೂ ಹೂಡಿಕೆಗಳೇ. ಅವು ಹೇಗೆ ಭಿನ್ನ?

objectives.en: Define human capital and human capital formation
Distinguish physical capital and human capital

narration.en: A factory buys a new machine; a family pays for a daughter to become a doctor. Both are investments that raise future output. In what way are they different?
narration.kn: ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆ ಹೊಸ ಯಂತ್ರ ಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ; ಕುಟುಂಬ ಮಗಳನ್ನು ವೈದ್ಯೆಯಾಗಿಸಲು ಖರ್ಚು ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಎರಡೂ ಹೂಡಿಕೆಗಳೇ. ಅವು ಹೇಗೆ ಭಿನ್ನ?

body.en: Just as a society turns physical resources like land into physical capital like factories, it can turn human resources like students into human capital like engineers and doctors. Human capital is the stock of skill and expertise of a nation at a point of time. Human capital formation is the process of adding to it over time through investment in education, health and training.
body.kn: ಭೌತಿಕ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲಗಳು ಭೌತಿಕ ಬಂಡವಾಳವಾಗುವಂತೆ, ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳಂತಹ ಮಾನವ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲಗಳು ಎಂಜಿನಿಯರ್, ವೈದ್ಯರಂತಹ ಮಾನವ ಬಂಡವಾಳವಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಒಂದು ದೇಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದು ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಕೌಶಲ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಿಣತಿಯ ಸಂಗ್ರಹವೇ ಮಾನವ ಬಂಡವಾಳ.

narration.en: Human capital is the skill and knowledge in people. Each extra year of education raises earnings by a rate of return, just as a machine raises output. Physical capital can be sold; human capital stays with the person. Compare 10 and 15 years of schooling at a 10% return. Does the extra lifetime income cover the years not spent earning?
narration.kn: ಮಾನವ ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಜನರಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಕೌಶಲ ಮತ್ತು ಜ್ಞಾನ. ಯಂತ್ರ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುವಂತೆ ಪ್ರತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ವರ್ಷ ಆದಾಯವನ್ನು ಪ್ರತಿಫಲ ದರದಷ್ಟು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಭೌತಿಕ ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಮಾರಬಹುದು; ಮಾನವ ಬಂಡವಾಳ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಿಯೊಂದಿಗೇ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ. 10% ಪ್ರತಿಫಲದಲ್ಲಿ 10 ಮತ್ತು 15 ವರ್ಷ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ. ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಜೀವಮಾನ ಆದಾಯ ಗಳಿಸದ ವರ್ಷಗಳನ್ನು ತುಂಬುತ್ತದೆಯೇ?

title.en: On the board: Two kinds of capital

say.en: A society turns land into factories: physical resources become physical capital.
In the same way, education turns students into engineers and doctors: human capital.
Compare them. Physical capital can be sold; human capital stays with its owner.
Both depreciate, but skills can be kept up by continuous learning and health care.

text.en: Tangible: can be seen and touched
Can be sold in the market
The skills of a trained nurse
Intangible and inseparable from its owner
Built by spending on education and health
Benefits society as well as the owner

explanation.en: Physical capital is tangible, saleable and mobile. Human capital is the skill and knowledge in people: intangible, part of its owner, and with benefits that spread to others.

body.en: Physical capital is tangible and can be sold in the market; human capital is intangible and is inseparable from its owner. Physical capital is mobile between countries, while human capital moves less easily because of nationality and culture. Both depreciate, but human capital can be kept up by continuous investment. Human capital benefits the owner and also society, through external benefits.
body.kn: ಭೌತಿಕ ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಮೂರ್ತ, ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾರಬಹುದು; ಮಾನವ ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಅಮೂರ್ತ, ಅದರ ಒಡೆಯನಿಂದ ಬೇರ್ಪಡಿಸಲಾಗದು. ಮಾನವ ಬಂಡವಾಳ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಿಗೂ ಸಮಾಜಕ್ಕೂ ಲಾಭ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: Classify each as physical or human capital: (a) a tractor, (b) a nurse's training, (c) a school building, (d) a programmer's coding skill.

steps.en: (a) Tractor: tangible, can be sold: physical capital.
(b) Nurse's training: skill inseparable from the nurse: human capital.
(c) School building: tangible structure: physical capital (it helps create human capital).

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Classify each as physical or human capital: (a) a tractor, (b) a nurse's training, (c) a school building, (d) a programmer's coding skill.

body.en: Ask: "Can I sell it without selling the person?" If yes, it is physical capital; if no, it is human capital.

mnemonic.en: Can it leave the owner? Yes = physical, No = human

narration.en: Spot human capital fast. Ask: "Can I sell it without selling the person?" If yes, it is physical capital; if no, it is human capital.
